title: An affine model has a population projection
notes: CORE · 4 min explanation. Teaching purpose: Under independent standard-normal inputs, the best unregularized affine predictor is 1+2x0. Mechanism and worked reasoning: E[x1²]=1 and Cov(x1,x1²)=0 by symmetry. The intercept absorbs 1 while the linear x1 coefficient cannot recover the even curvature. Finite Ridge is not exactly this population projection. Ask: Why can the x1 coefficient be near zero despite x1 mattering? Expected explanation: A symmetric square has no population linear covariance with x1. A small affine coefficient does not mean the nonlinear input is irrelevant. Visual interpretation: Analytic population projection under independent standard-normal inputs; finite Ridge differs. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. Live laboratory blocks include discussion and navigation through reference pages; do not time every page again. title: A residual curve has a conditional mean
notes: CORE · 3 min explanation. Teaching purpose: With e=prediction−observation, the population affine residual mean is 1−x1². Mechanism and worked reasoning: At x1=0 the mean residual is +1; at x1=±2 it is −3. Finite fitted residuals also contain coefficient estimation error and observation noise. Compare both candidates on identical test rows and scales. Ask: Does the curve alone prove physical causation? Expected explanation: No. The generator is known in this constructed example. An observational residual pattern suggests hypotheses; it does not identify a physical causal mechanism. Visual interpretation: Analytic population conditional residual, not a fitted sample. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. title: Noise and misspecification are not the same
notes: CORE · 4 min explanation. Teaching purpose: Independent observation noise has zero conditional mean; a missing square does not. Mechanism and worked reasoning: For the best affine population projection, error=1−x1²−epsilon. Independence gives MSE=Var(x1²)+Var(epsilon)=2+0.04=2.04. The exact quadratic oracle has MSE 0.04. Ask: Is 0.04 an exact score for every finite test sample? Expected explanation: No. It is the expected squared observation noise under the stated generator. A finite fitted model and finite test sample add estimation effects and sampling fluctuation. Visual interpretation: Population calculations for the declared synthetic generator; finite fitted test scores differ. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. Live laboratory blocks include discussion and navigation through reference pages; do not time every page again. title: Refit variation requires actual refits
notes: CORE · 4 min explanation. Teaching purpose: One residual scatter plot mixes several effects and cannot identify training-sample variance. Mechanism and worked reasoning: For each n = 40, 160, 640, fit each family on 20 independent training draws. Predict the same240 noise-free probe points. Within a repetition, use paired rows for both families and sample sizes. Ask: Why use noise-free probe targets? Expected explanation: The known signal removes new test-label noise from this comparison. Training noise still affects fitted coefficients. The spread across fits measures variation over the declared training sampling procedure. Visual interpretation: Actual fresh fits on declared synthetic samples; shaded bands are ±1 refit SD, not predictive intervals. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. title: An empirical decomposition can be checked
notes: REFERENCE · use during practice / no extra lecture time. Teaching purpose: Mean squared signal error = empirical bias² + refit variance. Mechanism and worked reasoning: At each probe point subtract and add the mean of 20 predictions. The cross-term sums to zero. Average across probe points; use ddof=0. Add 0.04 only for a noise-averaged expected label error. Ask: Must every estimated component decrease monotonically with n? Expected explanation: No. Finite repetitions and regularization can make local fluctuations. Interpret the paired experiment and uncertainty; do not manufacture a smooth trend or claim the estimated mean is the exact population mean. Visual interpretation: Actual notebook outputs, fixed 240-point noise-free probe and 20 refits; ddof=0. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. Live laboratory blocks include discussion and navigation through reference pages; do not time every page again.
